PipelineModel.title: PipelineModel
PipelineModel.description:
Root model for Orchestra pipeline definitions.

Orchestra pipelines are DAGs (directed acyclic graphs) of task groups that orchestrate jobs
across external systems (dbt, Snowflake, Fivetran, Databricks, AWS, GCP, Azure, etc.).

DAG structure: The 'pipeline' dictionary contains task groups (recommended) or standalone tasks.
Each entry has a user-chosen ID that can be referenced in 'dependsOn' arrays. Task groups are
the primary mechanism for building DAGs -- dependencies between groups define execution order.

Variable system: Use ${{ expression }} syntax throughout the pipeline. Available variable types:
- ENV.*: Environment variables (e.g., ${{ ENV.MY_VAR }})
- ORCHESTRA.*: Global runtime variables -- PIPELINE_RUN_ID, CURRENT_TIME, TASK_RUN_ID
- inputs.*: Runtime inputs (e.g., ${{ inputs.my_input }})
- matrix.*: Matrix iteration values (e.g., ${{ matrix.table_name }})
- ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS['task_id'].OUTPUTS['name']: Upstream task outputs
Built-in functions: format_date(timestamp, format, timezone), add_days(timestamp, delta),
add_months(timestamp, delta), len(list), int(value), str(value).

Trigger model: Triggers use OR-logic -- any single trigger firing (cron schedule, webhook,
pipeline event, or sensor) starts a pipeline run.

Pipeline run states:
Created -> Running -> Succeeded | Failed | Warning | Cancelling -> Cancelled.
Task run states:
Created -> Queued -> Running -> Succeeded | Failed | Skipped | Cancelling -> Cancelled.

Key constraints: Task IDs must be unique across the entire pipeline. Dependencies must not be
circular. JSON keys use snake_case in YAML but are converted to camelCase in the API (except
in 'parameters' blocks and 'inputs').

parameters.description: Integration-specific parameters for the check.

mapOutputs.title: Mapoutputs
mapOutputs.description: Maps check result fields to pipeline input names. Keys are pipeline input names, values are output field references from the check result.

SensorCheckModel.title: SensorCheckModel
SensorCheckModel.description:
Defines a single check within a sensor.

Sensor checks query external systems (e.g., Snowflake, S3) to determine if
conditions are met. All checks in a sensor must pass for the sensor to trigger
the pipeline.

SensorCheckSchemaResponse.title: SensorCheckSchemaResponse
SensorCheckSchemaResponse.description: Metadata and parameter schema for a sensor check type.

name.title: Name
name.description: Sensor name for display and reference (max 100 chars).

cron.title: Cron
cron.description: AWS EventBridge cron expression defining when the sensor evaluation window opens. Same 6-field format as schedule cron.

timeoutMins.title: Timeoutmins
timeoutMins.description: Maximum minutes to wait for all checks to pass (max 7200 minutes). Must be shorter than the interval between cron invocations.

environments.title: Environments
environments.description: Environment(s) to run in when sensor triggers.

checks.title: Checks
checks.description: Dictionary of sensor checks that must all pass. At least one required.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Expression evaluated after all checks pass, before triggering the pipeline. Uses ${{ expression }} syntax.

exclude.title: Exclude
exclude.description: List of dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to skip sensor evaluation.

frequencySecs.title: Frequencysecs
frequencySecs.description: How often checks are evaluated within the open window, in seconds (60-600, default 60).

runInputs.title: Runinputs
runInputs.description: Input values to pass when sensor triggers pipeline.

SensorModel.title: SensorModel
SensorModel.description:
Defines a sensor that monitors external systems and triggers a pipeline when conditions are met.

Polling model: The cron expression opens a check window. Within the window, checks are
evaluated at frequencySecs intervals (default 60s). The pipeline triggers when ALL checks
pass, or the timeout is reached. Triggers use OR-logic — any single trigger (schedule,
sensor, webhook, or triggerEvent) firing starts a pipeline run.

SingleIntegrationAuthResponse.title: SingleIntegrationAuthResponse
SingleIntegrationAuthResponse.description: Integration auth response including the full credential parameters.

StartPipelineResponse.title: StartPipelineResponse
StartPipelineResponse.description: Response returned when starting a pipeline.

StateApiModel.title: StateApiModel
StateApiModel.description: Full state snapshot for a connection's tracked resources.

StateItem.title: StateItem
StateItem.description: Tracks the state of a resource with a checksum and source timestamps.

TaskDurationAboveBaselineData.title: TaskDurationAboveBaselineData
TaskDurationAboveBaselineData.description: Anomaly data for a task run whose duration exceeded its baseline.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: Dictionary of task definitions within this group. Must have at least one.

dependsOn.title: Dependson
dependsOn.description: IDs of other top-level pipeline entries (group or standalone task IDs) that must complete before any task in this group runs. This is how the DAG is constructed -- dependencies between groups define execution order.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Expression using ${{ expression }} syntax applied to ALL tasks in the group. Combined with task-level conditions via AND. Example: "${{ tasks['upstream_task'].status == 'SUCCEEDED' }}".

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for the group (max 100 chars).

matrix.description: Matrix configuration for running the group multiple times with varying inputs. Reference values in tasks via ${{ matrix.<input_name> }}. Each value spawns a parallel child iteration of the entire task group.

TaskGroupModel.title: TaskGroupModel
TaskGroupModel.description:
Defines a group of tasks that execute together within a pipeline.

Task groups are the primary DAG building block. Dependencies between groups create the
execution graph -- even single tasks should be wrapped in groups. Groups can have matrix
configurations to run multiple iterations with different input values. Group-level
conditions are combined (ANDed) with task-level conditions.

integration.description: The integration platform (SNOWFLAKE, DBT, AWS_ECS, etc.).

integrationJob.description: The operation to perform. Must be compatible with the integration.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Integration specific parameters. Structure depends on integration_job.

dependsOn.title: Dependson
dependsOn.description: IDs of tasks or groups that must complete before this task runs. Dependencies are typically set at the task group level to define the DAG structure. Use an empty array [] when relying on group-level dependencies.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Expression using ${{ expression }} syntax that determines whether this task runs. If combined with a group-level condition, both are ANDed together. Examples: status-based "${{ tasks['task_1'].status == 'SUCCEEDED' }}", input-driven "${{ inputs.flag == True }}", time-based "${{ format_date(ORCHESTRA.CURRENT_TIME, '%d') == '01' }}", output-based "${{ ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS['task_id'].OUTPUTS['results'] == 'val' }}".

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for display in UI (max 100 chars).

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Labels for filtering and organization (max 10 tags).

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Named connection to use for this task's integration. Format: 'name_XXXXX' pattern with trailing 5-digit suffix (e.g. 'my_snowflake_12345'), or a variable expression '${{ ENV.CONNECTION_NAME }}'.

operationMetadata.title: Operationmetadata
operationMetadata.description: Additional integration configs for lineage tracking.

treatFailureAsWarning.title: Treatfailureaswarning
treatFailureAsWarning.description: If true, task failure results in WARNING status instead of FAILED.

configuration.description: Task-specific retry/timeout settings. Overrides pipeline-level configuration.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Alerts to send when the task completes.

TaskModel.title: TaskModel
TaskModel.description:
Defines a single task within a pipeline that runs a job on an external integration.

Tasks trigger jobs in external systems (dbt, Snowflake, Fivetran, etc.) and handle
monitoring, metadata, and configuration automatically. Task run states:
Created -> Queued -> Running -> ((Succeeded | Failed | Skipped) | (Cancelling -> Cancelled)).

TaskRunArtifactsResponse.title: TaskRunArtifactsResponse
TaskRunArtifactsResponse.description: List of filenames associated with a task run.

TaskRunFile.title: TaskRunFile
TaskRunFile.description: Metadata for a file attached to a task run.

TaskRunFilesResponse.title: TaskRunFilesResponse
TaskRunFilesResponse.description: List of filenames and file metadata associated with a task run.

TaskRunResponse.title: TaskRunResponse
TaskRunResponse.description: Full details of a single task run within a pipeline run.

TaskRunStatus.title: TaskRunStatus
TaskRunStatus.description:
NOTE: if changing these values, please also confirm the AWS Step Function state machine
is not impacted. This can be done by looking at `terraform/modules/step_function/main.tf`, and
viewing the state machine JSON definition.

type.title: Type
type.description: Event type. Currently only 'pipeline' is supported.

pipelineId.title: Pipelineid
pipelineId.description: UUID of the pipeline whose completion triggers this pipeline. If 'ANY', triggers on any pipeline completion.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: List of pipeline run statuses that trigger this pipeline. Available values: SUCCEEDED, FAILED, WARNING, CANCELLED. If omitted, triggers on SUCCEEDED and WARNING only.

runInputs.title: Runinputs
runInputs.description: Input values to pass to the triggered pipeline run.

TriggerEventModel.title: TriggerEventModel
TriggerEventModel.description:
Defines a pipeline completion event that triggers this pipeline.

Enables pipeline chaining where completion of one pipeline automatically
triggers another. Can filter by completion status. Triggers use OR-logic --
any single trigger firing starts the pipeline.

wildcardParent.title: Wildcardparent
wildcardParent.description: When trigger_type is TRIGGER_EVENT, whether this hop matched only a wildcard (*) parent dependency edge.

TriggeredByApiModel.title: TriggeredByApiModel
TriggeredByApiModel.description: Describes what triggered a pipeline run (schedule, sensor, webhook, etc.).

WebhookRequestData.title: WebhookRequestData
WebhookRequestData.description: Full webhook request body for triggering a pipeline run.
